Digimon World 2 Online Tools

Info on these pages comes from the original Digimon World 2 (PS1), plus the balance changes and info from DW2 Online. I’ll keep updating it as things change.

DNA Digivolve
  • Add parents: enter two Champion, Ultimate or Mega Digimon to see what they make, or one and press Possible combos.
  • Find combos: enter the Digimon you want in Result name, then open it to see every pair of parents that makes it. Use Parent includes to show only combos that use a certain Digimon.
  • Reading combos: each combo has a group of Digimon on each side of the +. Any Digimon from the left plus any from the right gives the same result.
  • Result stage: the result is one stage below the parents. Two Champions make a Rookie, two Ultimates make a Champion and two Megas make an Ultimate. With mixed stages, it’s one stage below the lower parent: Mega + Champion makes a Rookie.

Add parents

Add two to see the result. Add one and press Possible combos to see everything it can make.

Find combos

Result name
Parent includes
 

Parents at different levels: the higher parent is first brought down to the lower one’s level, as if it were DNA Digivolved with itself. The result then comes from the two same-level Digimon. Example: Apemon (Champion) + Etemon (Ultimate). Etemon + Etemon = Ogremon (Champion), so Apemon + Etemon gives the same result as Apemon + Ogremon, which is Tapirmon.

Mutations are special results that break the normal pattern:

  • M-Tyrannomon, MetalGreymon, Whamon or Zudomon + Cherrymon = Vademon
  • H-Kabuterimon + Baihumon, M-Garurumon, P-Mamemon or SaberLeomon = SandYanmamon
  • H-Kabuterimon + Gryphonmon or Rosemon = Yanmamon
Vaccine (green)Data (blue)Virus (red)
Digipedia

Every Digimon’s family tree, from Rookie to Mega. Tap a name to open its info card, which shows its type, specialty, weaknesses, moves and digivolutions.

  • Levels: a Digimon digivolves at EL 11 (Rookie to Champion), EL 21 (Champion to Ultimate) and EL 31 (Ultimate to Mega).
  • DP (Digivolve Points): where a tree branches, the game picks the branch whose DP badge matches your Digimon’s DP. “any DP” means there is only one branch. DP goes up by 1 each time you DNA Digivolve.
Stages, left to right as it grows: Rookie → Champion → Ultimate → Mega

DigiBank

Keep track of the Digimon you have. Your bank is saved in this browser.

  • Add: pick a Digimon and fill in what you know, including moves it knows. Only the name is needed.
  • DNA Chain: press Fill from DigiBank there to use your bank. Press Send to bank on a Digimon there to save it here.
  • Favourite: tap the star on a card. Favourites show first.
  • Fresh: tick it for a Digimon that has never been in a battle. Only Fresh Digimon can be sold on the Digimon Marketplace.
  • Teams: battles are 3 v 3. Build teams below to see their type and specialty matchups.
  • Move it: copy your bank code to use the same bank and teams on another device.

Add a Digimon

Import from a CSV file

A spreadsheet file with one Digimon per row. It reads the columns by their names: Name, Level, MaxLevel, HPmax, MPmax, ATK, DEF, SPD, DP, Quality and EXP (HP and MP work too). A Digimon with 0 EXP and 0 DP is marked Fresh. HPmax and MPmax are used as its HP and MP; current HP, MP and EXP aren’t stored.

DNA Digivolve in your DigiBank

Pick two of your Digimon (Champion or higher) and press DNA Digivolve to see the result. Nothing changes until you add it.

    DNA Chain

    Finds the shortest chain of DNA Digivolves and level-ups from the Digimon you have to the one you want, with the moves you choose.

    1. Add the Digimon you have, with their DP. Max level, Quality and known moves are optional.
    2. Pick the Digimon you want and any moves it should end up with.
    3. Press Find shortest route. Each step shows what to combine or level up, and the DP, Max level and Quality that result.

    Not sure what to aim for? Press What can I make right now? Save a setup under Saved chains to come back to it or share it.

    Saved chainsSave this setup, or share it as a code▾

    Digimon you want

    Moves it should know by the end
    A DNA result starts at its stage’s first level (Rookie 1, Champion 11, Ultimate 21) with its own move and the strongest parent move it can use. The parents’ other moves go on its to learn list, and it learns the ones at its stage or lower at its next level-up (EL 2, 12 or 22). Higher-stage moves wait until it digivolves to that stage and reaches the normal move level (EL 12 Champion, 22 Ultimate, 32 Mega). A move still on the list is lost in a DNA, so steps marked with a red ! tell you to train a parent first. The final Digimon can keep a move on its list if its own line can still reach that stage.

    Digimon you have

    Must use: the route has to include that Digimon, for example to pass its moves down. Don’t use: leaves it out of the search for now, without removing it or changing your DigiBank. Moves: add moves a Digimon already knows, so the route can count them. Max level: leave it blank if you don’t know it, and the route won’t limit that Digimon by level.

    DigimonDPLevelMax levelQualityUse in search

    No Digimon match.

    Show as

    Rules the route follows

    • Shortest: the fewest DNA Digivolves first, then the fewest level-ups.
    • Quality: a DNA result takes the Quality of the parent with the higher Level when you DNA Digivolve, or the higher Quality if both Levels are the same. The route has you train each parent to its Max level first, so it compares their Max levels. Shown when you enter Quality. With Prefer the highest Quality ticked, the route tries to carry your highest-Quality Digimon through to the end, even if that takes more steps.
    • DP: a DNA result gets the higher parent’s DP + 1. Level-ups keep DP the same.
    • Max level: a DNA result’s Max level is the higher parent’s level + (the lower parent’s level ÷ 5), rounded down. The route assumes you train each parent to its Max level first.
    • Digivolve as far as it can: a Digimon trained to its Max level digivolves every time it can, so the route always uses its highest form as a DNA parent (when its Max level is known). This matters most for your main Digimon with DP 2 or more.
    • Train to Max level: always level each Digimon to its Max level before you DNA Digivolve it. It ends up with better stats, and the result gets a higher Max level.
    • Max levels you haven’t entered: the route works backwards from the end and shows the lowest Max level each of those Digimon (or new ones to get) needs, so every level-up in the chain is possible.
    • Level limits: a Digimon needs a Max level of at least 11, 21 or 31 to reach Champion, Ultimate or Mega. Max levels are only checked for Digimon you entered one for, and for lines made only from them.
    • Copies: each Digimon you added can be used at most once, and only if the route needs it. The route never asks you to get one you already have. If you have more than one, add each to the list.
    • No route: the route suggests Digimon to get, Rookies first, then Champions, then Ultimates. A Champion counts as two Rookies, and an Ultimate as five, so Ultimates only come up when they save a lot of steps. It never suggests the Digimon you want or any Mega. New Digimon start at DP 0, and their Max level isn’t tracked.

    Source: DNA Max level and Quality rules posted by Wyrelade on the DW2 Online Discord, and checked in game.

    DNA Stats

    Work out what a DNA Digivolve gives you: the new Digimon’s Max level, Quality and starting stats, and the stats it reaches at its Max level.

    1. Parents (optional): enter each parent’s name, Level and Quality to get the new Digimon’s Max level and Quality. Add both parents’ stats to also get its starting stats.
    2. New Digimon: its Quality, Max level and starting stats, filled in from step 1 or typed in yourself. Pick each stat’s growth class.
    3. Result: its stats at Max level, next to what Quality 0, Quality 100 and the original game would give.

    1Parents optional

    Parent A

    +
    Parent B
    Stats (optional, to work out the new Digimon’s starting stats)

    2New Digimon

    StatAt startGrowth
    Digivolves at level (leave blank if it won’t)

    Starting stats are the numbers on its status screen at the start level. Growth is the species’ growth class for that stat (A grows best). Each new stage restarts the big early Attack and Defense gains, and each digivolve adds 30 Max HP and 30 Max MP, so the digivolve levels matter.

    3Result

    NormalFineRarePerfect
    Chance of each level-up roll at this Quality
    Lowest gainLowHighHighest gain
    How much better (or worse) at Max level than another Quality, for example one you could DNA instead.

    DNA rules

    • Max level = the higher parent’s level + (the lower parent’s level ÷ 5), rounded down. Which slot each parent is in doesn’t matter (tested in game). Example: EL 15 + EL 13 gives 15 + 2 = 17.
    • Quality comes from the higher-level parent. If both are the same level, the result gets the higher Quality. Example: EL 15 (Quality 66) + EL 12 (Quality 87) gives Quality 66.
    • Starting stats come from both parents’ stats, rounded down. A Champion parent makes a Rookie: HP and MP 10% of both added together, Attack and Defense 40% of the higher + 30% of the lower, Speed 30% of both. Ultimate + Ultimate or Mega + Ultimate makes a Champion (34%, 50% + 30%, 45%). Mega + Mega makes an Ultimate (45%, 50% + 40%, 50%). Rookies can’t be DNA Digivolved.
    How Quality changes growth (details)
    • Better rolls: each level-up, every stat gains from one of 4 rolls, lowest to highest. At Quality 0 the chances are 50 / 30 / 15 / 5 %. At Quality 100 they are 5 / 15 / 30 / 50 %. Values in between scale evenly.
    • Bonus growth: every gain gets an extra Quality ÷ 10 %: +10 % at 100, +7.7 % at 77. Leftover fractions are saved and added in later.
    • Late levels: later in growth, Attack and Defense only rise on the best roll. Quality 0 gets it 5 % of the time and Quality 100 gets it 50 %, so high Quality keeps growing long after low Quality stops.
    • Not included: stat changes from digivolving itself, items and gear. Wild Digimon don’t show Quality; it’s set when one joins your party.

    Quality tiers and recruit odds (the exact value within a tier is random)

    Normal0 to 5958.64 %
    Fine60 to 8435.01 %
    Rare85 to 946.01 %
    Perfect95 to 100, foil effect0.34 %

    Tinker reroll: rerolls a Digimon’s Quality for 10,000 bits and 5 Microprocessors. Each tier above Normal is half as likely as it is on a recruit.

    Sources: Wyrelade’s Quality table and calculator, and the DNA rules Wyrelade posted on the DW2 Online Discord.

    Digimon Moves

    Every move a player Digimon can learn, with its stage, MP cost, power and side effects. Search for a move or a Digimon, filter by stage, kind or status, or tap a Digimon name in the table to see only its moves.

    Learning moves: each Digimon learns its move at EL 12 (Champion), EL 22 (Ultimate) or EL 32 (Mega), keeps its moves when it digivolves, and DNA Digivolving passes on the moves both parents have learned. The result starts with its own move plus the strongest parent move it can use at its stage (highest power, then MP cost). The rest go on its to learn list: it learns them as it levels up, but only moves at its stage or lower. Higher-stage moves wait until it digivolves to that stage and reaches EL 12 (Champion), 22 (Ultimate) or 32 (Mega). Moves still on the list are lost if it’s DNA Digivolved again before learning them. How much damage a move does is on the Damage Formula tab.

    Boss and wild-only moves

    No player Digimon learns these. Only bosses and wild Digimon use them, so they’re left out of the main list and the Damage Formula tab.

    Power shows “–” for moves that don’t deal damage. Move data comes from a community skill list, and the effects are summarised in my own words.

    Damage Formula

    How much damage a move does, and what each Digimon is weak to. Damage is fixed: the same attack in the same situation always does the same damage, with no random roll.

    The short version

    Damage starts from the move’s Power. Type, specialty and the battle floor each make it stronger or weaker, and then your Attack against their Defense scales it.

    Power×Type×Specialty×Floor (move)×Your Attack÷Their Defense × Floor (target)
    Worst case about ×0.51Neutral ×1.0Best case about ×2.16

    Best case: a type win and a specialty win, on a floor that matches your move and beats the target (1.2 × 1.2 × 1.2 ÷ 0.8). For example, a Water move on a Fire Digimon, on a Water floor. Worst case: a type loss, a specialty loss and a floor that beats your move (0.8 × 0.8 × 0.8). The game rounds down twice along the way, so results can be off by 1.

    Exact formuladamage = floor( floor(Type × Specialty × Power × FloorForMove) × Attack ÷ floor(Defense × FloorForTarget) )

    Attack and Defense are shown as whole numbers, but the game keeps decimals, which is why it can be off by 1.

    The four parts

    Type
    Your Digimon’s type against theirs: ×1.2 if yours wins, ×0.8 if it loses, ×1.0 if both are the same type.
    Specialty
    The move’s element against the target’s specialty: ×1.2, ×1.0 or ×0.8. No specialty is always ×1.0.
    Floor (move)
    The floor against your move’s element: ×1.2 on its own floor, ×0.8 on the floor that beats it. A Fire move is ×1.2 on a Fire floor and ×0.8 on a Water floor.
    Floor (target)
    The floor against the target’s specialty, applied to its Defense: ×1.2 on its own floor (you do less), ×0.8 on the floor that beats it (you do more).

    Floors follow the specialty wheel’s arrows both ways. Specialty itself doesn’t: its ×0.8 uses a separate chain (see Specialty below). So a Fire move is ×1.0 against a Water Digimon, but ×0.8 on a Water floor.

    Some moves change their own Power in certain situations, for example Transcend Sword goes from 50 to 75 against a target that’s countering. The formula then just uses the new Power. Each move’s description on the Digimon Moves tab says when this happens.

    Type

    VirusbeatsDatabeatsVaccinebeatsVirus
    Your type×1.2 against×0.8 against

    Type comes from the Digimon, not the move, so every move it uses gets the same type bonus.

    Specialty floors

    Coloured floor in a domain. If a battle starts while your Digi-Beetle or the enemy is on one, the whole battle uses that floor.

    Blue = WaterRed = FireGreen = NatureGold = MachineBlack = Darkness

    On its own floor, an element’s moves hit ×1.2 harder and Digimon with that specialty get ×1.2 Defense. On the floor that beats it, both are ×0.8. A Fire Digimon on a Water floor does less with Fire moves and takes more damage. A strip of coloured floor in a hallway usually means a boss is close.

    Specialty

    Each arrow points to the element it beats, for ×1.2. The ×0.8 matchups are a different chain, not the arrows backwards: Water → Nature → Darkness → Fire → Machine → Water. So a Fire move on a Water Digimon is ×1.0, but on a Machine Digimon it’s ×0.8.

    Target’s specialtyWeak to ×1.2Resists ×0.8

    DW2 Online changes

    Stat-down skills that hit all enemies last 3 rounds, don’t stack, and bosses take half the effect and never drop below 75%. Details and other balance changes are on the DW2Notes tab.

    Rows are the attacking element and columns are the target’s specialty. Green is x1.2, red is x0.8 and blank is x1.0.

    The move lists use damaging moves from the Digimon Moves tab, strongest first. Fighting on a floor of the move’s element adds another x1.2. If a Digimon isn’t on any list, its specialty hasn’t been confirmed yet.

    Sources: MetalKid’s Digimon World 2 FAQ (GameFAQs), Wikimon: Digimon World 2, StrategyWiki: Digimon World 2 Terms. The floor ×0.8 rule and the DW2 Online changes come from DW2 Online players and the patch notes.

    Patch Notes

    DW2 Online patch notes, newest first. Hotfixes are merged into the update they fixed, so nothing is listed twice.

    1.2.4Server, Digimon joining
    New
    • Room for more players: the player cap is raised from 420 to 600.
    • Smoother full servers: server network work now runs on several threads.
    Changes and fixes
    • Digimon joining: High-DP Digimon (DP 10+) need a stronger gift to join and join less often. Champions and Ultimates that need DP also join a bit harder.
    • Fixed a crash when typing in chat.
    • Fixed a crash with soft HD rendering on some Windows PCs.
    • Fixed PvP rematch sometimes never starting after both players pressed Rematch.
    • Gamepad now works in the Tinker and Digivolver lists.
    • Domain Connector list: hold D-pad or stick to scroll, right stick and L2 / R2 to page.
    • Boons: Digimon you fed no longer stay stuck as held or locked in the Digivolver lists.
    • Market: ROM Domain items no longer show as Abyss in the List window.
    1.2.1Digivolver, Domain Boons, Chat rooms
    New
    • Digivolver window with 3 tabs: Digivolve, DNA and Fuse. All Digimon are in one scrollable list instead of several pages.
      • Name search, sorting and filters: Ready / All / Rookie / Champion / Ultimate / Mega.
      • Digivolve shows all available evolutions and the DP required for each.
      • DNA select a parent to see the result with every other Digimon. A confirmation window comes before DNA, and a result card shows the old and new stats.
      • Digivolve and DNA animations are unchanged.
    • Shortcuts: Q / E or L1 / R1 switch tabs, and 1 / 2 / 3 jump to a tab.
    • Market: Digimon listed on the Market appear as locked.
    • Domain Boons (Tinker > Boons): feed spare Digimon to a domain to add a positive modifier.
      • Boon slots = the number of negative mods on the domain (minimum 1, maximum 3).
      • Cost: Lv 1–10 = 2 points, Lv 11–20 = 3, Lv 21–30 = 4, Lv 31+ = 5.
      • Points: Rookie 1, Champion 2, Ultimate 4, Mega 8. Maximum 24 Digimon per feed; extra points are lost.
      • Fill picks the cheapest Digimon. Each feed grants 1 random boon, and duplicate effects on the same domain are not possible.
      • When all slots are full, you can pick a boon to reroll it. The new roll can be worse.
      • Boons don’t raise Threat or reduce pay. Tuning a domain keeps its boons. Boons aren’t available on Glitched, Chaos Boss, Abyss, Miasma, Sanctum or Trinity domains.
      • Domains with boons can’t be sold on the Market. Party and Market Digimon can’t be fed.
      • Higher boon values unlock at domain levels 8, 18, 28 and 40.
    • Domain Merge (Tinker > Merge): merge 3 domains into 1 at no cost.
      • Level: the highest input level +1 if all 3 are within 5 levels of each other, otherwise the highest input level. Max level: your best clear +1.
      • Rare chance: 15% base, +10% per Rare input and +5% per Common input. The result is never Basic and takes its theme from one of the 3 inputs.
      • Generates new random mods. Boons on the input domains are lost. Glitched, special, chain, free and Market-listed domains can’t be merged.
    • Chat: Global chat is replaced by 4 rooms: ENG, BR, ES and ID.
      • /rooms, /join BR and /leave ES. Use /eng, /br, /es, /id or /1–/4 to send to a room.
      • Custom chat tabs (up to 6) with unread counts. Press Tab or click a tab label to change where you send.
      • Accented characters (ã, ç, é, ñ) are supported.
      • Speech bubbles are Local chat only. /ignore Name and /unignore Name, with an Ignored tab in the F window.
      • 10-second slowmode per room.
    • Other: an Ironman Removal NPC in the Tamer’s Club (free, cannot be undone). The Events window has Active and Ended tabs. World Boss end warnings at 60, 30 and 5 minutes. Race podium messages are orange. Palmon is back dancing in the Tamer’s Club.
    • Chaos DNA: Chaos-fused lines and their DNA children carry the Chaos DNA icon. Re-fusing costs less and gives no extra stats.
    Balance
    • Trinity: charges every 3 rounds. Member attack ×1.40 and member HP +15%. KO’d members skip their charge.
    • Maximum 1 fragment per Domain Boss victory.
    • Attack buffs now always last at least 1 action.
    • Twin Roll: recruit quality is rolled twice and the better result counts.
    Fixes
    • Fixed DNA desync after relogging.
    • Fixed loot being lost when leaving a domain through Esc > Leave Domain.
    • Fewer disconnects after lag spikes.
    • Android: switching apps mid-run no longer loses the run. Drag and pinch controls on the Mastery board, a PvP target touch pad, fixed chat typing, shop keyboard support, L / R switches between Chat and Map, and item links open by tapping.
    • Beetle station keeps the parts list after equipping.
    • Mastery points label shows the correct maximum.
    • Battle target shows the item name. Fixed Baihumon and Diaboromon skill names.
    • Mission chests correctly show “No loot in missions”.
    • Gamepad support for Commissions (Assign) and Tinker.
    • Steam Deck: pressing A no longer opens chat.

    1.1.0Nov 6, 2026Android, matchup info
    New
    • Android version with touch controls (on-screen pad, finger as mouse, drag and scroll), the phone keyboard for chat, and its own auto updater.
    • Chat Digimon links: Alt + click a Digimon in the Digimon window (U) to post it in chat. Others can hover the green link to see it and its model.
    • New battle skill window: skills sorted into tabs by kind, with full mouse and number key support. The classic window can still be picked in settings (F1).
    • Battle matchup info: battle plates show each Digimon’s Specialty icon and type. When choosing a target, arrows show whether your attack has the type and Specialty advantage.
    • Specialty icons in the Digimon window: in the header, the Specialty row and on every skill.
    • Commissions: the board shows your progress to the next rank (Merit and best clear level), and the window can now be opened inside a domain (it closes when a battle starts).
    • Market: new Type filter to search parts by slot.
    Fixes and changes
    • Promotion missions: you can’t join other players’ missions, only the boss win drops loot or domains, and enemies always refuse gifts.
    • A run is no longer lost when stepping onto the exit portal or stairs at 0 EP.
    • Market “My listings” shows the seller’s side of a sale: what you get and where it goes.
    • The Tinker Tune page shows the domain item’s Threat under its mods.
    • The Inventory item card follows the gamepad cursor in the bag and stash.
    • Better performance for big battle effects (like Nova Blast) on PCs without Vulkan.
    1.0.23 – 1.0.25Nov 5, 2026400 players, Menu Wheel
    New
    • Player cap raised to 400 (from 200).
    • Menu Wheel: open game windows from one wheel. Set it up in F1 > Controls: pick its gamepad button (Circle, L3, R3 or Off) and fill 8 slots with windows or leave them Empty, with a Default Slots button to reset. It also has a keyboard keybind under Interface. Windows opened from it work fully on a gamepad, and it never opens over another window.

    • Digi-Lab: Digimon past the first page can be reached again by scrolling. Going down or scrolling past the last row moves to the next page.
    • ClearAgumon is see-through again in the Digimon window, Digiline, station and other model pictures.

    1.0.22Nov 4, 2026Look Changer, Domain Tuning
    New
    • Tamer’s Club Look Changer: a new NPC left of the Tamer’s Club entrance. Pick from 35 tamer looks for 5,000 Bits per change. Other players see it right away.

    Stat-down skillsOct 25, 2026balance

    Two Okuwamon in one party made most fights trivial, so stat-down skills that hit all enemies changed:

    • Last 3 rounds instead of the whole battle.
    • Don’t stack: hitting a stat that’s already lowered only restarts the 3 rounds, so two Okuwamon do the same as one.
    • Bosses take half the effect, and their stats never drop below 75% of normal.
    • Cost more MP: Duo Scissor Claw went from 36 to 60 MP, and Tidal Wave and the other all-enemy stat-down skills went up too.
    • Single-target stat-down skills are unchanged.
    • Enemies using these skills follow the same rules.

    The Digimon Moves tab already uses these MP costs. Posted by Wyrelade on the DW2 Online Discord.

    Tips

    How DW2 Online works, grouped by topic.

    Starting outCharacter, faction
    • One character per account.
    • Your starter doesn’t lock your faction. You pick the faction separately, so you can start with Agumon and still join Black Sword.
    Your factionHQ, Merits, gifts

    Leave the Main Gate and your faction’s headquarters is on the town map.

    • Gifts: your faction decides which type of gifts you can buy from vendors. Toy gifts can’t be bought: they only come from chests, drops and other players on the Marketplace.
    • Merits are the faction currency. You earn them from Commissions and by clearing Domain Items.
    In the headquarters
    • Commissions: a quest board. You don’t need to accept anything; a message pops up when you finish one. Hand it in at the NPC so a new one appears. Rewards are Merits.
    • Quartermaster: sells for Merits. Always has your faction’s C, B and A gifts. A Glitched Domain and Digi-Beetle gear at your Tamer level change daily.
    • Leaderboards: faction rankings for domains cleared, highest domain level and Merits. Just for show, no rewards.
    • Leader’s Room: shows your Team Rank and what you need to rank up. Your rank shows on your profile, unlocks profile icons and gives Mastery Points.
    DomainsDomain Items, Mastery

    Use a Domain Item at the Domain Connector (Carol) to enter a randomly generated domain. You start with three permanent ones, one each of Vaccine, Data and Virus. Every other Domain Item is used up when you enter.

    • Losing a run: if you run out of EP or HP, or lose a battle, you’re sent back to the Main Gate but keep all the loot you found so far.
    • Summary window: after a run it shows your loot, battles won, EXP, Bits and Merits. You can salvage parts right there.
    What a Domain Item tells you
    • Level: the level of the wild and boss Digimon.
    • Type: the boss’s type. Wild Digimon are mostly that type too, but not always.
    • Rarity (Basic, Common, Rare): the most affixes it can have.
    • Affixes: mostly negative effects on the run. They raise the Threat level.
    • Threat level: more Threat means more and better loot, EXP and Bits.
    Getting more
    • Chests, wild Digimon, and the Marketplace.
    • Bosses always drop at least one.
    • Glitched domains are boss-floor runs with extra loot and EXP. The Quartermaster sells one each day, and some Mastery nodes make them drop more often.
    Mastery
    • Each Domain Item is named after its type, using names from the original game. Two items with the same name are still different domains.
    • Your first clear of each Domain Item gives 1 Mastery Point, and so does its Glitched version. Cleared ones have a green tick in the Domain Connector.
    • Each Team Rank also gives 1 Mastery Point. You can have up to 50 points in total.
    • Open the Mastery Tree with M. Clusters boost things like toy drops, Glitched domains and higher level domains, or make domains never have rock walls or spores blocking the way.
    • Your first reset is free; later ones cost resources and Bits. Plan it in the Mastery Planner tab.
    Weekly World BossEvent
    • Open it with the Event button in the bottom left of the Domain Connector, next to Masteries.
    • One attack per day: deal as much damage as you can in 5 turns.
    • When the server reaches a damage goal, everyone who joined in gets the same reward, no matter how much damage they did.
    Quality and DNAStats, Max level
    • Quality (0–100) decides how much your Digimon’s stats grow, so higher is better. 95–100 have a foil shine.
    • You can’t see a wild Digimon’s Quality. It’s set the moment it joins you.
    DNA Digivolution
    • Max level = higher parent’s level + lower parent’s level ÷ 5, rounded down. Example: 15 and 13 → 15 + 2 = 17. Which slot each goes in doesn’t matter.
    • Quality comes from the higher-level parent, even if the other has more. Example: Lv 15 Q66 + Lv 12 Q87 → Q66.
    • If both are the same level, the higher Quality is kept: Lv 15 Q66 + Lv 15 Q87 → Q87.
    • The DNA Chain tab uses these rules, and “Prefer highest Quality” plans around them.
    Digi-Beetle partsMods, crafting
    • You start with basic parts. Parts come in Basic, Common and Rare; rarer parts can hold more mods.
    • Mods only affect the Digi-Beetle, never your Digimon. “+25% Max HP” means the Beetle’s HP. Mods cover things like trap and spore damage, Break Resist and rare find chance.
    • Tiers: T5 is the lowest and T1 the highest. Higher tiers give bigger percentages.
    Crafting and salvage
    • Craft at the Digi-Beetle mechanic NPC. Crafting uses materials and rerolls a mod’s percentage.
    • Hold Alt on a part to see each mod’s range, e.g. T5 Break Resist 23% (19–25%).
    • Salvage parts you don’t want (right click > Salvage) for materials based on rarity. This also works in the summary window after a run.
    • Materials also come from chests, battles and the Marketplace.
    MarketplaceTrading
    • Sellers set their own price, and the buyer pays an extra Bits fee to complete the sale.
    • Digimon Marketplace: only Fresh Digimon can be listed, meaning ones that have never been used in battle. The fee goes up with the Digimon’s stage.
    PvPColosseum
    • Talk to Leomon in the Colosseum to see listed challenges and tournaments.
    • To make your own challenge, set the lowest and highest stage (Champion, Ultimate, Mega), a max level and your party, then wait for someone to join and accept.
    • PvP gives no rewards, only points for show.

    Source: tips posted by Halfwaynoob [tSR] and Wyrelade [GunZ] on the DW2 Online Discord.
